name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,485

clue.text: What itchy divers do to satisfy requirements

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: divers with an itch surface and then relieve it
second meaning: reach the expected standard

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what scuba divers with an itch do, dressed up as meeting a job's requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical literal reading of the idiom: divers rise to the surface in order to have a scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reach the expected standard, scratch being the old starting line in boxing and racing.

clue.text: Maybe Charlotte's frequently taking time out with good state institution

indicators.note: maybe flags that the named singer is one example of a family name we need
taking out the abbreviation for time means removing that single letter from the word before it

blocks.note: Charlotte Church is a Welsh singer; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A sentence about the singer Charlotte Church often taking time off from her good work.
explanation.walkthrough: CHURCH, then OFTEN without its T, then G and LAND: CHURCH OF ENGLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: The Church of England is the established national church, an institution of the English state.

clue.text: Fly in central Georgia

blocks.note: GE is the international code for the country Georgia

explanation.surface: Someone flies into the middle of Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb about air travel but it is the noun, an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny two-winged insect, a kind of fly.

clue.text: What one with the biggest mouth does is extreme

definitions.text: What one with the biggest mouth does

blocks.clueFragment: What one with the biggest mouth does
blocks.note: first meaning, split in two: the loudest talker speaks more than anyone

explanation.surface: A wry remark that the person with the biggest mouth always goes too far.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as UTTER MOST, the answer is what a loudmouth does: says the most.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttermost is an emphatic form of utmost, meaning at the furthest limit or greatest degree.

clue.text: Eats in mess for tea

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone eats in the canteen or officers' mess at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' looks like a dining hall, as in the army, but it signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a herbal infusion, a kind of tea made from flowers or leaves.

clue.text: Instruments Queen held on board ship

indicators.note: on board puts something inside a vessel, so these letters go between the two halves of the ship

blocks.note: pent means shut in or confined

explanation.surface: The Queen's musical instruments are kept aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword Queen. A serpent is an old snaking bass wind instrument, not a snake here.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent is a Renaissance bass wind instrument with a sinuous wooden body and a cup mouthpiece.

clue.text: Rectify title

blocks.note: second meaning: an entitlement or legal claim

explanation.definitionFit: To right something is to correct it, and a right is a legal title or claim to something.

clue.text: Members of the Royal Ordnance Military Band originally playing note on top of slide

definitions.text: Members of the Royal Ordnance Military Band originally playing note on top of slide

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so each word of the band's name gives only its opening letter
the top of a word in a down answer is its first letter

blocks.note: initial letters of these five words
on as in performing, on stage

explanation.surface: Band members of a military ordnance band play notes using slides.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: these band members play their notes on a slide.
explanation.definitionFit: Trombones are brass instruments played with a sliding tube, standard in military bands, so members of such a band.

clue.text: Keep your fingers crossed when Bob, for one, and a thespian go travelling

indicators.note: travelling sets the letters in motion so they arrive in a different order

blocks.note: Bob Hope, the comedian, is one example of someone with that surname

explanation.surface: Wishing for luck as Bob and an actor set off on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like part of the travel phrase, but it is also fodder, supplying the G and O.
explanation.definitionFit: To hope against hope is to keep hoping when the odds are poor, as when crossing fingers for luck.

clue.text: Latest news of US lawyer in illegal set-up

indicators.note: something illegal is bent or crooked, so the letters of the word after it are bent out of order
in places the lawyer inside the reworked letters

explanation.surface: Breaking news about an American lawyer caught up in an illegal sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set-up' reads as a frame-up, but it is just the five letters to be rearranged around DA.
explanation.definitionFit: Updates are the most recent pieces of information or news reports on a developing story.

clue.text: Shuffle about with family

blocks.note: a group or class of related things, as in biology

explanation.surface: Shuffling around with relatives, like a family gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shuffle about' looks like a phrase meaning shamble, but 'about' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To regroup is to rearrange or reorganise into new groupings, much as shuffling reorders cards.

clue.text: Permission for demolition

blocks.note: first meaning: official authorisation, as for take-off

explanation.surface: Someone seeks planning permission to knock a building down.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance is authorisation to proceed, and also the clearing away of old buildings from a site.

clue.text: I chewed over a bone

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters before it are read backwards

explanation.surface: A dog's boast: I gnawed on a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger of the two bones in the lower leg.

clue.text: Choice work with metal including a bit of osmium

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here just its opening letter
including means the metal holds the extra letter inside it

blocks.note: its first letter, also osmium's chemical symbol's first letter

explanation.surface: A choice of working with metals, including some osmium.
explanation.walkthrough: OP is the usual abbreviation for opus, a work.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is something one may choose, an alternative available to select.

clue.text: Rear window and another car part

blocks.note: the tail is the rear end
a light is a pane or window

explanation.surface: Listing car parts: a rear window and something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear window' looks like a single car part, but it splits into two synonyms; the answer is the other car part.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail light is the red lamp at the back of a vehicle, a different component from the rear window.

clue.text: Georgia's capital welcomes a group of Italian players

indicators.note: a city that welcomes someone takes them in, so the city's name holds the extra letter

blocks.note: the capital of the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Atlanta hosts a visiting Italian team or band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' sounds like musicians or actors, but Atalanta is a football club from Bergamo.
explanation.definitionFit: Atalanta is a Serie A football club based in Bergamo, a team of Italian sportsmen.

clue.text: Weight put on first magnet

indicators.note: first tells us the second phrase's word is placed ahead of the first one

blocks.note: to put cargo on is to load
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Something heavy is set on top of a magnet.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A loadstone (lodestone) is naturally magnetised iron ore, the original natural magnet.

clue.text: His padre converted Spanish jew

indicators.note: converted means changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A priest converts a Spanish Jew to Christianity, recalling the Inquisition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' fits the religious picture perfectly, which hides its role as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sephardi is a Jew of Spanish or Portuguese descent, from the Hebrew name for Spain.

clue.text: Letters of stone seen in European houses

indicators.note: seen in means found inside, so the stone's abbreviation goes within the houses

blocks.note: a pile is a large stately house

explanation.surface: Letters carved in stone are on show in great houses across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: A pile is a large imposing house; ST is the abbreviation for stone the weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistles are formal letters, especially the apostolic letters of the New Testament.

clue.text: Cleric's hand over when first son becomes rector

indicators.note: becomes swaps one letter for another, and first picks the earlier of two matching letters

blocks.note: to pass on is to hand over

explanation.surface: A clergyman hands over his parish when his eldest son becomes rector.
explanation.walkthrough: PASS ON has two S's; only the first changes to R, giving PARSON.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a parish priest, a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Northern Australian adult in toilet with Noah's grandson

indicators.note: in places the three single letters inside the word for a toilet

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, as in film ratings

explanation.surface: An Australian from the north is stuck in a toilet with a biblical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Canaan is the son of Ham, who was one of Noah's three sons.

clue.text: Outbursts during yoga lesson

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: Fits of laughter or frustration break out in a yoga class.
explanation.definitionFit: Gales can be bursts of laughter, as in gales of laughter, sudden noisy outbursts.

clue.text: Room letters regularly overlooked in small town

indicators.note: overlooking letters at regular intervals means skipping every other one

blocks.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: In a small town, a room where letters lie unread.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a reception room or drawing room in a large house.

clue.text: Better chance of success following destruction of Death Star

indicators.note: destruction breaks something to pieces, and the pieces are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: The rebels' prospects improve once the Death Star from Star Wars is destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an advantage at the outset, giving someone a better chance of winning.

clue.text: Look for athletic power we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is identified by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: abbreviation, as in AC for Athletic Club
weight means influence or power, as in carrying weight

explanation.surface: Seeking an athlete's strength, so it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to wait for it, to look for or expect its arrival.

clue.text: Bony with a collapsed lung and a touch of rheumatism

indicators.note: something collapsed has fallen apart, so its letters are rebuilt in another order
a touch is just a small part, here only the opening letter

blocks.note: the article and the organ, taken as written

explanation.surface: A thin, bony patient suffers a collapsed lung and some rheumatism.
explanation.definitionFit: Angular describes a lean figure with sharp, prominent features, much like bony.

clue.text: Fruit and veg originally by food delivery company

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so each of the two words before it gives its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of these two words
Ocado is a British online grocery delivery firm

explanation.surface: An online grocer delivers fruit and vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit and veg' reads as one phrase, but 'and' supplies a letter. Ocado is a British online supermarket.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is botanically a fruit, a large berry with a single stone.

clue.text: Holding back engineers receiving European money for prison

indicators.note: receiving means the engineers are given the money, which sits next to them

blocks.note: detention is keeping someone back, as after school
a cent is a hundredth of a euro
Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers are paid in euros to build a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A detention centre is an institution where people, such as young offenders or migrants, are held: a kind of prison.
